item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Thu Feb 25, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Conducting Qualitative Thematic Analysis Without Coding — Thu Feb 25, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Thematic analysis is a widely used and useful approach for analyzing qualitative data, but developing themes does not have to involve coding. This workshop introduces alternative, creative approaches to thematic analysis that invite researchers to engage deeply with qualitative data through practices such as annotation, close reading, and poetic analysis. Participants will explore how to identify patterns of meaning, to attend to language and expression in data, and to develop interpretive insights without relying on a formal coding process. Through examples, discussion, and hands-on activities, participants will experiment with ways of engaging with their data, including noticing resonances and tensions across data and using poetic techniques to explore and emphasize the meanings, emotions, and experiences expressed in qualitative materials.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Feb 26 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Partner Yoga: A Practice for Two — Sat Nov 28, 4:30 PM — Yoga Off East
item.description:
NOTE: Your registration covers TWO people (yourself + your guest). Only one person of the pair needs to register. In this workshop, we invite you to discover and explore what it takes to practice yoga asana with another person. Whether you come with a significant other, bestie, yoga buddy, or family member, practicing partner yoga is always a lot of fun. We open the practice by being together, breathing together, and creating connection. Then we practice many familiar yoga poses in partnership – doing some poses together and giving each other hands-on adjustments and assists in others. This practice is a safe place to laugh, build trust, and be curious. Often participants say that it teaches us about communication not only with our own bodies but with those of other people. Please join us after our studio session has concluded to enjoy a cup of tea! To get a glimpse into what partner yoga looks like check out our video https://youtu.be/pQIOxHE0sW8.

These tools can be used to summarize textual documents through AI-assisted memo writing and to support coding, with each program taking a different approach to integrating human judgment and AI features.
The course will also demonstrate how ChatGPT can be used to code textual data, how to create effective prompts, and how to import results from ChatGPT into qualitative software for further analysis. item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Feb 25 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.
